Subject: Approval needed: Senior Runtime Engineer offer & comp band

Hi Kim / Marcus,

Quick ask — we have a strong candidate (Alex Chen, referred by TalentBridge) for Senior Runtime Engineer on the kernel team. After loop with hiring managers and a short take-home, manager recommendation is positive and they'd like to move to offer. Details below: 

- Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (IC4/IC5 boundary in our leveling)
- Team: Kernel / Serving (reporting to Marcus)
- Proposed band: L5 (Comp band midpoint $190k, range $170k–$215k) — manager requests flexibility toward top of band because of relevant low-latency systems experience and production GPU runtime background.
- Target start: late June (candidate has a 4-week notice)
- Recruiter: Elena Markova (TalentBridge)

I've attached the draft offer packet and the comp-band matrix for Q2. Requesting:
1) Approval to extend an offer up to $210k base (total comp conversation to follow)
2) Confirmation on whether we can do a 10% sign-on to bridge notice period (one-time payment)
3) Headcount confirmation: this would use the existing kernel open HC (slot K-09 in our runtime slate).

If you want a short sync, I can jump on the phone — otherwise please reply with approval/changes.

Thanks,
Sean

Thanks Sean — quick clarification items before I sign off: 

1) You listed L5 but you referenced "IC4/IC5 boundary" in the note. Please confirm the exact leveling recommendation from Marcus (L4/L5/L6 labels in our comp doc).
2) If manager is asking to go above midpoint to $210k, remind me of the business justification (must tie to scarcity, direct impact on our latency SLOs, or runway risk).
3) Would the team be willing to use the Q2 hiring tranche that has a slightly higher comp flex budget? If so, we may need to mark this as "conditional approval" until finance signs the tranche shift.

Assuming Marcus confirms level and we document the impact, I can approve up to $205k base today and a discretionary sign-on up to 8% (subject to final outbound offer language). Anything above that needs Marcus + compensation committee signoff.

Kim

Kim / Sean — thanks for the note. Manager recommendation is for L5 (Senior). A few data points for the justification: 
- Alex has 4 years building inference pipelines with optimized KV cache management and a track record of shaving 10–15% tail latency at 99th pct at his current employer.
- We're in active roadmap work to reduce GPU utilization on multi-tenant pools and this hire will own the kernel-level optimizer. High leverage.
- Benchmarks from the interview loop showed above-average latency optimization skills and good production debugging.

Regarding tranche: we can pull from the kernel slot K-09 which is allocated to kernel feature hires but the comp-flex buffer is limited. If Kim can approve $205k + 7% sign-on we can close quickly; otherwise we'll need comp committee for $210k.

Happy to join a quick 15-min sync if that helps unblock. 

Marcus
